Answer: B. LDL

LDL (Low-Density Lipoprotein) is the primary transporter of cholesterol to peripheral tissues. It delivers cholesterol to cells via LDL receptors, which can lead to plaque formation in arteries. HDL (High-Density Lipoprotein) facilitates reverse cholesterol transport, removing cholesterol from tissues. VLDL (Very Low-Density Lipoprotein) primarily transports triglycerides, while IDL (Intermediate-Density Lipoprotein) is an intermediate step in the metabolism of VLDL to LDL. Thus, LDL is the main carrier for cholesterol delivery to peripheral tissues.
